doc.title: Jon Hendricks interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Ellington's wish to match Fletcher Henderson; Lunceford's show band
summary: Duke Ellington wanted only to approach Henderson's band; Hendricks recalls Lunceford's costume changes in Toledo.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Well even Ellington had his influences, and that kind of pulled a lot of things together to make his sound.
I was surprised when he told me that all he wanted to have was an orchestra that would approach Fletcher Henderson’s. I said whoa.

Yeah, I think he did. But I mean that’s what he wanted. He just wanted to approach Fletcher’s orchestra. That makes you want to go back and listen to Fletcher again. But © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -6-

that was a clean band. They were beautiful. And Jimmie Lunceford’s too, he also admired Jimmie Lunceford’s band, because they dressed well. I saw them one time in Toledo in a show — they had three costume changes. They opened up in white tails, they came back in the middle in orange tuxedos, and they closed in light tan tuxedos. Great show band, it was really fantastic. A really good looking outfit too, and entertaining, very entertaining.
